title: Validate Binary Search Tree - Comparison
oneLinerQuestion: Compare how a valid BST passes vs how an invalid BST fails boundary checks.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Validate Binary Search Tree problem requires determining if a binary tree satisfies the Binary Search Tree (BST) property: for every node, all nodes in its left subtree must have strictly smaller values, and all nodes in its right subtree must have strictly larger values. Checking only the immediate children of a node is insufficient, as a node deep within a left subtree could violate an ancestor's upper bound. To enforce this globally, we propagate dynamic upper and lower value boundaries (min, max) down the recursion tree, ensuring every descendant strictly satisfies its inherited domain constraints.

- Step 1: Recursive Helper Definition — We define a helper function `validate(node, min, max)` that verifies whether the subtree rooted at `node` is a valid BST within the open interval `(min, max)`.

- Step 2: Base Case (Empty Subtrees) — If `node === null`, an empty tree is trivially a valid BST, so we return `true`.

- Step 3: Boundary Violation Check — We inspect the current node's value: if `(min !== null && node.val <= min) || (max !== null && node.val >= max)`, the node breaks the BST ordering condition, and we immediately return `false`.

- Step 4: Left Subtree Validation — When traversing into the left child (`node.left`), all descendant values must remain strictly less than `node.val` while preserving the inherited `min` bound. We recursively call `validate(node.left, min, node.val)`.

- Step 5: Right Subtree Validation — When traversing into the right child (`node.right`), all descendant values must remain strictly greater than `node.val` while preserving the inherited `max` bound. We recursively call `validate(node.right, node.val, max)`.

- Step 6: Initial Call & Root Execution — We initiate the traversal at the root with unbounded constraints: `validate(root, null, null)` (or using `-Infinity` and `+Infinity`). The tree is valid if and only if both subtrees recursively return `true`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the total number of nodes in the binary tree, as each node is visited at most once. Space Complexity: O(H) auxiliary stack space, where H is the height of the tree (O(log N) for a balanced tree, O(N) in the worst-case skewed tree).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isValidBST(root):
    FUNCTION validate(node, minVal, maxVal):
        IF node IS NULL THEN RETURN True
        IF node.val <= minVal OR node.val >= maxVal THEN RETURN False
        RETURN validate(node.left, minVal, node.val) AND validate(node.right, node.val, maxVal)
    END FUNCTION
    RETURN validate(root, -INFINITY, INFINITY)
END FUNCTION
